title: GPU slop consolidation and key-index audit: runtime patch to stop memory bleed and kvcache tombstone skew
creator: Diego Morales
description: Customer escalations across Hosted and Dedicated clusters surfaced a new memory-pressure pattern: intermittent GPU OOMs tied to a small but persistent allocator "slop" that accumulated across long-lived sessions, combined with stale tombstones in the KV cache index. The behavior manifests as gradual memory creep on nodes servicing high-concurrency chat workloads and eventually triggers allocator eviction storms that cause latency spikes and OOMs. This ticket tracks diagnosis, a minimal runtime hotfix to reclaim slop and reconcile the kvcache index, validation on private/Dedicated environments, and an ops rollout with rollback criteria.
impact_summary: Multiple customers in Hosted and Dedicated experienced degraded throughput and soft OOMs during peak periods. Two enterprise customers reported sustained failures for 10-30 minutes with failover to fallback model variants. Customer impact: high. Business impact: SLA blips and escalations to CSMs.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a dedicated node pool with mixed session longevity (many long-running sessions + burst clients).
2) Run synthetic chat load with variable prompt sizes and periodic KV writes (prefix caching + session pinning).
3) Observe memory usage: small steady increase in GPU resident memory over multiple hours, followed by sudden allocator eviction waves and OOMs when concurrent requests spike.
4) Collect heap/exported allocator stats and kvcache tombstone metrics and reproduce locally on a scaled-down dedicated node with same runtime config.
mitigation_actions: Applied temporary rate-limiter to highest-traffic routes to reduce burst concurrency (rolled out to Hosted).
Activated emergency per-tenant memory backpressure in Dedicated (throttles long-running sessions).
Deployed a disabled-mode patch for kvcache cleanup to run as a manual job to remove stale tombstones on most affected hosts.
proposed_fix: Runtime hotpatch: introduce a GPU slop-consolidation pass that collapses ephemeral arena fragments every N allocation cycles and returns freed pages to the main allocator instead of leaving small fragments resident.
KV index audit routine: compact tombstones and reconcile key-index deltas in the kvcache during low-traffic windows, with idempotent checkpointing to prevent double-apply.

Defensive metrics and guards: add TLS/trace points for allocation lifetimes and tombstone create/delete latency; add an automated canary that runs consolidation in read-only mode to validate correctness before enabling writes.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotpatch to release branch with feature flag defaulted to off.
2) Nightly canary in staging: run consolidation in read-only/observe mode for 24h and validate memory trend metrics do not regress.
3) Canary on 5% of Hosted traffic with write-enabled consolidation and kvcache audit; monitor for error rates, latency, GPU mem usage, and tombstone reconciliation counters.
4) Expand to Dedicated test tenants with existing friction profile; run sweep jobs and validate tenant-level memory smoothing.
5) Full rollout with gradual ramp over 48h if canary is green; rollback immediately on >5% increase in 5xxs or >10% regression in p99 latency.
monitoring_checks: GPU resident memory slope (tokens/min) per host
Allocator free-slot fragmentation metric (new slot fragmentation ratio)
KV cache tombstone lag and reconcile rate
Error rate and latency p95/p99 for impacted routes
OOM count and evict-wave frequency per host
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible steady-state memory creep after 72h on canary hosts under representative load.
KV index audit reduces tombstone lag by >90% in affected hosts without data loss.
No increase in application-level errors or model output regressions attributable to the patch.
Rollout runbook validated and rollback path tested in staging.
